🍁 Central Montréal, every building standing in 2016 by year of construction — 1860 → 2016.

Old Montréal comes first. Between the 1880s and the 1930s, rows of plexes with outside staircases filled the Plateau and the working-class districts, then a second wave came after the war. In the 1960s Place Ville Marie (1962), the metro (1966) and Expo 67 brought in the modern city, and the Olympic Stadium followed in 1976.

📊 Data: Ville de Montréal open data (CC BY 4.0), property assessment roll of every municipality on the island, with 2016 rooftop footprints completed by Bâtiments 2D where tiles were missing. 74% of years come from the roll; 26% are estimated (placeholder years 1875–1910 spread block by block, or the year of neighbouring buildings). Heights from floor counts, exaggerated.
🌍 Map: OpenStreetMap contributors.
